answers.rationale: B is the lower-cost, earlier-arriving nonstop after Erin's 9 a.m. call, with comparable fare flexibility. The small savings from a one-stop do not justify adding connection risk, and United loyalty is only a tiebreaker when otherwise comparable.

B preserves Erin's preferred later-day travel pattern, has a short manageable connection, arrives slightly earlier than A, and costs less. D's very early departure is unnecessary for a travel-and-check-in-only Monday, while C's long layover and later arrival are not worth its modest savings.

B is the best-value afternoon nonstop: it is cheaper and arrives earlier than the comparable United nonstop, while avoiding Frontier's weaker bundled-fare trade-offs. The 10:15 departure is unnecessarily close to the 9 a.m. call and gives up Erin's established preference for afternoon departures when there is no operational need to leave early.

A is the afternoon nonstop that best matches Erin's stated preference when Monday is only travel and check-in. With no reception or early-arrival requirement and every option reaching the hotel before dinner, the small fare advantage of the earlier United nonstop does not outweigh the less convenient schedule; the connecting options add unnecessary complexity.
